recentItems.title: The Journalists Who Witnessed 9/11 25 Years Ago
recentItems.description:
On September 11, 2001, journalists across the eastern United States raced toward a story no one had imagined. From Washington, DC, to Pennsylvania and New York, they tried to make sense of events as they unfolded. 

Nearly 3,000 people died. A nation was forever changed. Among those journalists was Mike Walter. Twenty-five years later, he sits down with fellow reporters who were there – to remember that day and what it was like to tell the story while living through it.

recentItems.title: How some Western media used a Washington DC house to smear China's disaster response | Pointcast
recentItems.description:
What happens when tragedy becomes a media narrative? In this latest edition of Pointcast, Liu Xin speaks with Hong Kong-based author and journalist Nury Vittachi about media coverage of the devastating landslides near Gyirong Port in southwest Xizang, China, along the China-Nepal border. As rescue efforts continued following the disaster, some Western media reports raised questions about the scale of the damage and accused China of suppressing information. Liu Xin and Nury Vittachi take a closer look at these claims, examining what may have been overlooked in the reporting and how tragedy can become entangled with broader political narratives about China. What did the media reports miss? What do the facts on the ground tell us? Watch the full conversation and share your thoughts in the comments.
#Xizang #GyirongPort #ChinaNepalBorder #Landslide #NaturalDisaster #WesternMedia #CGTN #ThePoint #LiuXin

Guest
Nury Vittachi
Editor of Hong Kong's "Friday" news project

recentItems.title: AI, ready to provide services?
recentItems.description:
AI can write, create and chat for us. That's hardly news anymore. At the China International Fair for Trade in Services (CIFTIS) 2026, AI is upgrading with new services: moving from answering to functioning, and from standalone applications to computing power and models delivered across borders. How much can AI really do? And how is AI reshaping the future of trade in services? Let's find out!

recentItems.title: 37 boatmen, 6 boats, 7 days: How the Red Army crossed the Jinsha River?
recentItems.description:
It was one of the most critical moments in the Long March. In May 1935, after months of grueling travel, the Red Army reached the Jinsha River – a major natural barrier on its journey north. At Jiaoping Ferry, 37 local boatmen and six wooden boats played a crucial role in helping more than 30,000 Red Army soldiers cross the river. #LongMarch90
